name: Spring Security 6/7 authorization extension points for OPA
description: Spring Security has no native ABAC; integrate OPA via its extension points: (1) custom AuthorizationManager<RequestAuthorizationContext> for HTTP request-level checks; (2) AuthorizationManager<MethodInvocation> for method-level pre-auth (wire as an AuthorizationManagerBeforeMethodInterceptor @Bean Advisor); (3) custom annotation @OpaPreAuthorize(action) for declarative type-safe checks; (4) custom beans callable from SpEL. Spring Security 7.0 renamed AuthorizationManager.check() to authorize(). Build as a standalone starter — the Spring team's recommended pattern; ABAC-in-core was declined (issue #4276).

name: Pluggable claim extractor: JWT -> AbacContext.Subject
description: Don't hardcode token/claim shapes. Define an extractor interface (Authentication -> AbacContext) and ship a default JWT implementation, letting consumers override claim mapping (roles claim, attribute claims). Keeps the library usable with any IdP (Keycloak, Okta, custom) instead of one provider's claim names.

name: Pre-authorization decorator that also removes a redundant resource load
description: Pre-fetch the resource being authorized once, run the ABAC check against it, cache it request-scoped, and let the handler reuse the cached resource instead of re-SELECTing it. This both centralizes the check and removes one DB read per authorized request. Make it opt-in/flag-guarded per handler so behavior is byte-identical when off (handler falls back to its own load+check), enabling gradual rollout.

content: Auto-configuration must be conditional and overridable: gate beans on @ConditionalOnClass / @ConditionalOnProperty, and every bean with @ConditionalOnMissingBean so consumers can replace it. Bind config via @ConfigurationProperties with safe defaults. Register via META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports.

description: The @OpaPreAuthorize pointcut used AnnotationMatchingPointcut.forMethodAnnotation (checkInherited=false), so an annotation declared on an INTERFACE method was never matched under class-based (CGLIB) proxies — Spring Boot's default. The method ran with no enforcement and no error: the worst authz failure mode (looks protected, isn't). The manager's own findAnnotation searched interfaces, masking the gap in any test that exercised the manager directly instead of the pointcut.
resolution: Use new AnnotationMatchingPointcut(null, Annotation.class, true) — checkInherited=true searches the type hierarchy, same posture as Spring Security's own @PreAuthorize pointcut. Pin with a slice test that proxies with setProxyTargetClass(true) and annotates only the interface method. General rule: any custom method-security pointcut must be tested under CGLIB with interface-declared annotations.

title: Generalize fetch-authorize-cache as AbacResourceResolver SPI + request cache; do not port a central class-keyed rule registry
rationale: A central registry presupposes a uniquely-typed command object per operation (a mediator) for total, type-safe class->rule lookup. Vanilla Spring MVC's dispatch unit is the controller method, so a registry degrades to method-name/pointcut keys: runtime-only binding, two sources of truth, no compile-time link. Co-located @OpaPreAuthorize annotations ARE the rule table; the SPI supplies what they lack (resolved instance attributes).

description: spring-boot-starter-opa-abac example-user-management; fixed f453e12; found by retro-audit 2026-06-12.
resolution: Three-part fix: (1) privileged codes are unassignable through general endpoints (single-owner invariant routes through a dedicated transfer flow that atomically downgrades), (2) the guard compares the capability ladder in addition to resource permissions (SubsetGuard.requireAssignableByActor), (3) sweep the MIRROR operations (demote/strip the owner) in the same pass.
